body.statement: If \(\mathrm{oeq:global\text{-}endpoint\text{-}response}\) is resolved affirmatively, Theorem 5 supplies a finite constant \(C\) such that \[\rho_n^\ast\le C\left(\frac{\log n_\ast}{n_\ast}\right)^{s/(2s+d)}.\] Together with Theorem 6, this gives the conditional matching frontier \[c\left(\frac{\log n_\ast}{n_\ast}\right)^{s/(2s+d)}\le\rho_n^\ast\le C\left(\frac{\log n_\ast}{n_\ast}\right)^{s/(2s+d)}.\]
body.justification: This proposition isolates the only endpoint-response-dependent part of the minimax frontier from the unconditional lower theorem.
body.gap: Existing smooth optimal-transport estimation rates do not yield a global cross-Hessian margin test; the upper inequality follows only after the boundary-uniform endpoint response is established.
body.consumer: Analysts obtain the exact attainable order once the stated analytic endpoint question is settled, without weakening the unconditional impossibility result.
